== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|The House, also known as [[Valinhall]], is an incomprehensibly vast and mysterious entity that functions as more than a mere collection of buildings. Unlike the standard dwellings found in villages like [[Myria]], which are constructed from wood or clay, [[the House]] is a self-contained world that contains entire landscapes and lacks external windows or doors. It possesses the ability to rearrange its internal layout and generate new rooms based on the requirements of those living within it. The interior is incredibly diverse, ranging from grand, expensive chambers and [[throne]] rooms to naturalistic environments like caves, forests, or endless fields of ice. Some areas serve specific functions, such as gardens that provide essential food and [[water]], while others appear to have no clear purpose. The House is inhabited by various beings, including [[the Nye]], who are fundamentally bound to it, and it has historically been governed by powerful individuals who provided structure and identity to its residents. While it can be a source of peace and luxury, [[the House]] is also described as potentially deadly and capable of being under attack. It is a sentient-like environment that can be influenced by certain objects or individuals, and it possesses a [[scale]] so immense that some of its floors are vast enough to have their own horizons.}}

== House of Blades ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|The House is a unique structure that possesses no exterior. Inside, it features an artificial sky overlooking a massive fruit tree and a pool capable of healing wounds. [[The Nye]] are bound to this location, which has also provided [[Simon]] with various prizes. Ultimately, [[Simon]] contemplates the possibility of escaping into [[the House]].}}

== The Crimson Vault ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|The House is an incomprehensibly vast domain whose [[entry hall]] can be observed through the Gate. Within its many halls, individuals such as [[Simon]] have been known to run, and it serves as a location associated with [[Kai]] and others. While [[Incarnation|the Incarnation]] possesses an unlimited supply of nearly all [[the House]]'s powers, certain members of the institution view the actions of [[Valinhall]] as being aligned with [[Incarnation|the Incarnation]].}}

== City of Light ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|The House served as the location where [[Simon]] once received his training and later became a place he passed through. While [[Kai]] used to spend his days lounging around the residence, he also possessed the ability to banish [[Mithra]] within its walls. [[Leah]] noted that [[the House]] was a place she could follow the King into, though it is distinct from the source of power [[Simon]] calls upon.}}
